report.tagline: The UK's biggest property website, where home hunters search for free and estate agents pay a monthly fee to list homes.
report.simpleSummary: Rightmove is the website most people in the UK use to look for a house or flat to buy or rent. Searching is free. Estate agents and housebuilders pay Rightmove every month to show their homes there, because that is where the buyers are. It is one of the most profitable websites in Britain: it keeps about 70p of every pound it earns as operating profit.

overview.whatItDoes: Rightmove runs the UK's leading property portal for homes for sale, homes to rent, new builds and commercial property. Consumers search for free. Estate agents, letting agents and developers pay a monthly subscription to list properties and buy add-on products that make their listings stand out. It also earns from mortgage and rental services.
howItWorks: Estate agents send all their listings to Rightmove automatically from their software.
Home hunters search by area, price and features, save searches and get instant alerts.
A buyer or tenant contacts the agent through the listing; this enquiry is a lead for the agent.
Agents pay a fixed monthly membership per branch, plus add-ons like Featured Property and Premium Listings.
Homeowners use the free online valuation tool, which sends them to local agents who want to win the sale.
Ask Rightmove, an AI search tool, lets people describe what they want in plain words.
overview.valueProposition: For movers: almost every home on the market in one place. For agents: the largest audience of active buyers and sellers, so a listing gets seen and a sale gets won.

businessModel.summary: Rightmove makes money almost entirely from estate agents and housebuilders paying a monthly subscription to list homes, plus extra for add-on products. Consumers pay nothing. Because the site costs little to run and agents feel they must be on it, most revenue turns into profit.

revenueStreams.detail: Monthly fees from estate and letting agent branches; the biggest share of revenue.
Fees from housebuilders for developments; weak in 2026, which cut revenue guidance.
Featured Property, Premium Listings and other promotions.
Mortgages, rental services, commercial property and data products.

businessModel.pricing: Not public as a full price list. Agents pay per branch per month; estimated average revenue per advertiser is around £1,500 to £1,600 a month. In 2025 some agents reported price rises of around 12%.
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take one agent branch paying about £1,600 a month, so about £19,000 a year. Serving that branch costs Rightmove little: listings upload automatically and the site is already built. With an operating margin near 69%, Rightmove keeps roughly £13,000 of that as profit. For the agent, if Rightmove helps win just one or two extra sales a year at a £3,000 to £4,000 fee each, the subscription pays for itself, which is why agents complain but stay.

howTheyGetUsers: Brand: 'on Rightmove' is how people say a home is for sale

whatBringsUsersBack: Browsing as a hobby, sometimes called property porn
growth.moat: Rightmove has a strong network effect. Buyers go where the homes are, and agents list where the buyers are. Rivals like Zoopla and OnTheMarket have tried for years to break this, but agents cannot afford to leave Rightmove, which lets it raise prices. Its biggest risk is AI search tools becoming the new starting point.

pmLessons: A strong network effect lets a business raise prices, but pushing too hard invites rivals, regulators and lawsuits.
Free for one side, paid for the other works when the free side is the reason the paying side shows up.
Even leaders must invest when the way people search changes, as Rightmove is doing with AI.
Show paying customers their return, or they will only see the bill.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Rightmove revenue without raising agent fees?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at new revenue: mortgages, rentals services, seller tools, data. Size each and pick one with a metric.

interviewQuestions.question: AI chatbots start answering home searches. What should Rightmove do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Threat vs chance. Options: build Ask Rightmove, partner with AI tools, protect data. Track share of searches starting on Rightmove.

interviewQuestions.question: Agents are angry about fees. How would you measure the risk of losing them?
interviewQuestions.hint: Retention by agent size, leads per £, sentiment, rival offers. Define early warning signals.

interviewQuestions.question: Improve the Rightmove app for first-time buyers.
interviewQuestions.hint: Persona, their journey, top pains like speed and affordability. Ideas: affordability filter, instant viewing booking. Metric: enquiry rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is Rightmove's margin so high, and can it last?
interviewQuestions.hint: Network effect, low cost to serve, pricing power. Threats: legal claim, AI, CoStar. Give a view.

assumptions: The ARPA estimate of about £1,600 a month is extrapolated from 2024 figures and has not been confirmed for 2026.
The £3,000 to £4,000 agent fee per sale is a typical UK figure, used for illustration.
The 69% margin is calculated from H1 2026 underlying operating profit and revenue.
Package names like Optimiser are from earlier company materials and may have changed.
